newsitem.title: UK: Air Canada wins Heathrow handling contract.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada wins Heathrow handling contract.

text.p: Air Canada said it has won two new cargo handling contracts with Air China and Uzbekistan Airways at London Heathrow airport.

Air China currently operate two B747 flights a week between Beijing and London with a weekly import and export tonnage of around 80 tonnes. From next April, the airline will more than double its cargo capabilities when it begins four flights a week, three with B747 combi aircraft and one B747-400.
Uzbekistan Airways is currently operating A310s four times a week between London and Tashkent with monthly cargo volumes of up to 100 tonnes.
Air Canada's existing cargo handling contracts include Gulf Air, Royal Jordanian, Air Mauritius and Continental Airlines.

In 1996 Air Canada increased air cargo volumes at its two Heathrow cargo terminals where around 55 percent of freight handled was its own and 45 percent was handled for the contract carriers. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
